Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

S056 · The sanctuary’s reserved anointing oil

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

30:22 The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

30:23 “Take spices: five hundred shekels of the choicest myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty, and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane,

30:24 five hundred sanctuary shekels of iris, and a hin of olive oil.

30:25 Make these into holy anointing oil, a compound prepared by a perfumer’s skill. It shall be holy anointing oil.

30:26 With it anoint the Tent of Testimony and the ark of the testimony,

30:27 the lampstand and all its utensils, and the incense altar,

30:28 the altar of whole burnt offerings and all its utensils, the table and all its utensils, and the basin and its base.

30:29 Consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Everyone who touches them shall be sanctified.

30:30 Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.

30:31 Tell the sons of Israel: ‘This shall be holy anointing oil for you throughout your generations.

30:32 It shall not be applied to human flesh, and you shall not make anything like it for yourselves according to this composition. It is holy and shall be a holy thing to you.

30:33 Whoever makes anything like it, or gives any of it to an outsider, shall be destroyed from among his people.’”

Exodus 30:22–33

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Sanctuary, priesthood and ministry

Original scope: Text and setting: Sanctuary instruction

Connection to Christ: Hebrews supplies a broad sanctuary-to-Christ connection, while James describes anointing the sick; neither turns this recipe into a universal Christian formula. Christian response today: Treat worship reverently and distinguish Israel’s reserved oil from other legitimate uses of oil.

S057 · Incense reserved for worship

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

30:34 The Lord said to Moses, “Take to yourself spices: stacte, onycha, fragrant galbanum, and clear frankincense, in equal portions.

30:35 They shall make them into incense, a perfumer’s compound, blended, a pure and holy work.

30:36 Grind some of it fine and place it before the testimonies in the Tent of Testimony, where I will make Myself known to you. It shall be most holy to you.

30:37 You shall not make incense for yourselves according to this composition. It shall be a holy thing to you for the Lord.

30:38 Whoever makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall perish from among his people.”

Exodus 30:34–38

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Sanctuary, priesthood and ministry

Original scope: Text and setting: Sanctuary instruction

Connection to Christ: Revelation associates incense with the saints’ prayers; that image does not require reproducing the Mosaic incense recipe. Christian response today: Pray faithfully and avoid presenting a particular sacred mixture as necessary for Christian prayer.
